So viral that they expanded to 4 outlets now!!! 😆💥 

Have heard so much about @user ‘s kaya toast & Hokkien mee, it was saved in my must try list for a year now!! 

Truly lived up to the hype 🫡✊🏻 their kaya toast was toasted till it had a gd crunch (can rival Ya Kun’s) & their kaya was cold and spread across super generously!!!!! Rly solid 

Their Hokkien mee was as claimed, smoky, wokhey and umami but can be quite gelat if ur eating it alone. I preferred their prawn paste cutlet fried rice, my first time eating har cheong gai 🐣🍗 very fragrant! 

This place is officially on my top 3 kaya toast list in SG, we also saw eatbook host there (he claimed that this is top fav restaurant so far 👀) hahahaha

text:
22-course yakitori…fine dining style! A culinary homage to the great chicken! Yakun is new to LA in Sawtelle and offers a Japanese yakitori omakase in an intimate, elevated setting. 

The $280 pp experience starts with appetizers like sashimi, abalone, a5 wagyu, steamed egg and miso black cod. Then, it transitions into skewers that highlight all the different parts of the chicken! FYI you won’t find beef skewers here! But you will get a few non-chicken courses like asparagus and burdock root (some of my favorites). You end with dessert, which was an incredible crown melon, and they send you home with what’s by far the best take-home gift I’ve ever received from a restaurant, a traditional Japanese wind chime. 

#losangelesfood #sawtelle #yakitori #omakase #finedining

We had to try this Singaporean favourite in Tokyo!

Our verdict: As close to the local taste as it can get!
• Kaya was from the jar but understandable as they ship it from Singapore
• Taste of the Japanese half boiled egg was HEAVENLY
• Teh Peng was LEGIT, tasted like a kopitiam 

Also, because it’s Japan, each diner has to order something. So I ordered an apple juice 🤣🤗 

The Kaya Toast Set was ¥1,050 ($8.36), but still, a great fix for Singaporeans living in Japan. We were also surprised to see Japanese girlies eating dinner there!! 

☕️ Yakun Kaya Toast Japan 
📍 Tokyo International Forum
⏰ 8am to 8pm

text:
KAYA TOAST 😍 I had to give this traditional dish a go when in @user Singapore ! Is this the best place to get Kaya Toast?🧐

Kaya toast consists of Kaya spread (a sweet coconut & pandan spread) with a thick layer of butter in toast. It’s eaten with super soft boiled eggs and usually a coffee on the side! 🍞 

It’s a traditional Malaysian and Singaporean dish, very common in cafes around Singapore! 🥥 

I first headed to Heap Seng Leong to try it as this is one of the oldest and highest rated establishments. However I couldn’t bring myself to eat there as it was quite dirty 😭 I’m so sorry!!! I also realised it wasn’t halal certified nor were there any statements about it being halal-friendly so I took this as a sign to try elsewhere!

I then visited @user who have a few branches- their Beach Road branch was nice with outdoor seating and it was close to my hotel @user and @user 👌🏼 

I orders Set A (S$6 / ~£3.50) with Kaya toast, soft eggs and a drink. They said coffee was their signature so I got that, but you can choose any drink 🥚 

The coffee was actually nice and not too strong ☕️ 

I didn’t love the combo of the Kaya toast dipped in the eggs but I LOVED the Kaya toast itself. It was so good! With a lovely sweet coconut flavour and creaminess from the thick layer of butter 🧈 

My only regret was not buying some Kaya spread to take home 😢

You have to check out Kaya Toast when in SG! 🤤 

#halalfoodsingapore #kayatoast #yakunkayatoast

text:
📍Ya Kun Kaya Toast
18 China St, #01-01, Singapore 049560

💬 The "Green Plate" Ya Kun. The only Ya Kun with their bread toasted with Charcoal.
⁣⁣
📝 Unbiased Review⁣⁣
+ Set A Kaya Butter Toast [$6.30] 
+ Kaya butter toast was light and crispy with good spread of kaya and 2 slabs of butter. Balance was great, but we tasted no significant difference between the charcoal version and the normal version. If you were to blind taste them, it would probably difficult to tell them apart. 
+ Teh C had a traditional fragrance and creaminess we'd expect.
+ Eggs were still consistently good in quality and doneness. 
- French Toast [$3] served with kaya, this was dense, and the toast was unimpressive textually. The Kaya felt abit too sweet and the overall bite is sweet with no prominent standout features. 
- Insanely long queues under the sun as you wait for unfamiliar tourists to make their decision on the drinks to order.
- Tourist trappy as the cashier asks if we want the drinks to be in "this size" and points to only larger size cup on display, there was no original sized cups on the counter, so believe most tourists would just opt the large one. And it was true, majority around us were large iced cups and large hot drink cup. Wild.

⭐️4/5 (Traditional nanyang breakfast, no notable difference in charcoal toasting method. Most other Ya Kun, you would not be queuing under the sun. Slight tourist trap as they will push the upsized drinks.)

💬 The "Green Plate" Ya Kun. The only Ya Kun with their bread toasted with Charcoal.
⁣⁣
📝 Unbiased Review⁣⁣
+ Set A Kaya Butter Toast [$6.30] 
+ Kaya butter toast was light and crispy with good spread of kaya and 2 slabs of butter. Balance was great, but we tasted no significant difference between the charcoal version and the normal version. If you were to blind taste them, it would probably difficult to tell them apart. 
+ Teh C had a traditional fragrance and creaminess we'd expect.
+ Eggs were still consistently good in quality and doneness. 
- French Toast [$3] served with kaya, this was dense, and the toast was unimpressive textually. The Kaya felt abit too sweet and the overall bite is sweet with no prominent standout features. 
- Insanely long queues under the sun as you wait for unfamiliar tourists to make their decision on the drinks to order.
- Tourist trappy as the cashier asks if we want the drinks to be in "this size" and points to only larger size cup on display, there was no original sized cups on the counter, so believe most tourists would just opt the large one. And it was true, majority around us were large iced cups and large hot drink cup. Wild.

⭐️4/5 (Traditional nanyang breakfast, no notable difference in charcoal toasting method. Most other Ya Kun, you would not be queuing under the sun. Slight tourist trap as they will push the upsized drinks.)

✅ If you're single, eat half the toast as part of your breakfast and keep the other half as a pre-workout or tea break snack
✅ If you have a partner, share the toast with your partner
✅ If you want to up your protein count & keep your nutrition more balanced, buy an extra set of eggs
✅ If you want to lower your calories further, just opt for coffee or tea with no milk nor sugar

Either way, the above 4 tips will get you a reduced calorie count for your toast set so you can continue to enjoy your yakun experience without giving up on the toast.

text:
🧈🍳 Ya Kun Kaya Toast @user Gallery

- Traditional Kaya Toast (8/10)
kita pesen yang set (include Teh Tarik dan Soft-Boiled Egg)! For the kaya toast itself, dapet yg crispy spread with selai srikaya yg rasanya gurih dan slightly sweet! but, the amount of the kaya jam nya gak terlalu banyak. and also, the butter, makes everything balanced! we assume mereka pake butter yang salted (tp rasa asinnya very light).

- Soft-Boiled Egg (8/10)
setiap pesen, soft/hald boiled eggnya, selalu wonder how could they make the texture sooo perfect :) rasanya juga gurih & gak amis, makin comforting kalau ditambah kecap asinnya + lada putih!

- Iced Teh Tarik (8.5/10)
for the Teh Tarik… omg, very foamy, thiccc, tehnya jg berasa bgt, dan slightly sweet (less sugar), very likey!! btw, utk Traditional Kaya Toast set ini, only include hot teh tarik, we added +20k ish utk upgrade jd iced (karena porsinya bs 2x lipat :))

text:
Craving the Ya Kun Kaya Toast I had in SG last year 😭 it was sooo guud, so I ended up making my own at home~

I used Luvitaho’s kaya spread recipe.

Ingredients:
50 g palm sugar  
30 g granulated sugar  
200 ml coconut milk  
2 pinches of salt  
3 pandan leaves  
4 egg yolks  
1 tsp vanilla extract  

Serve with soft boiled eggs & teh tarik ☕🥚  
Instantly feels like I’m back on vacation.

text:
Their portion sizes were so large that me and my friend needed to take almost everything home.
It completely destroyed the stereotype that you can't get full at a fine dining place that I had. 
	
Everything from the sofa we sat on from the moment we walked in to every piece of tableware felt so exquisite

The ginger candy on the pre-dinner drink cup was so delicious 🤤, just like the old-fashioned ginger candy.
The Mocktail Sakura Grapes actually had a cherry blossom shower 🌸.

The chawanmush came with a Hello Kitty fish cake 🍥,

The chicken soup that came with the Wagyu Don smelled so fresh, just like the homemade fish stew I make at home.

🍈The fruit for dessert 😍, who even thought of eating melon after eating yakitori? 

The yakitori, was grilled to perfection.
I was so busy eating I forgot to take a lot of pictures since it was too tender, and juicy!!!😭
	
They have a pretty solid selection of Japanese cocktails 🍸, and a number of non-alcoholic options too.
	
The menu changes daily, with adjustments made based on the ingredients available for the day.
	
It's right next to the crepe shop on Sawtelle Millet, tucked away so you'd easily miss it. I never noticed it before, but the actual entrance is actually quite big.
📍YAKUN
2000 Sawtelle Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90025
🅿️Valet is $10, but you can also street park. Save where you can, spend where you should 
	
It was delicious, but I was just way, way too full 😭and you can even get more rice if you need it.
Before I came, I said I was so hungry I was going to eat everything in this pot!
Reality: couldn't finish it. I'll just have some rice soup with the broth 
I'm was literally comatose from how much I ate 🤣
#LA #losangeleslife #yakitori #omakase #foodie

text:
Our first food in Singapore, of course, Kaya Toast with soft-boiled eggs and iced kopi from Ya Kun Kaya in Parkway Parade!

If you want to experience Singapore's breakfast, look for Ya Kun Kaya, Toastbox, or food stalls in hawker centers that sell Kaya Toast. Kaya is a sweet coconut jam. A classic kaya toast consists of 2 slices of toast slathered with butter and kaya, typically paired with soft-boiled eggs. Best to enjoy it with a cup of kopi - I prefer iced kopi, given Singapore's hot weather.

text:
A rather indulgent breakfast sandwich, beloved in both Singapore and Malaysia.

Ingredients

Brown Kaya
Coconut milk (ideally 100% coconut) - 400ml
Eggs - 2 large
White sugar- 150g (split into 120g and 30g)
Pandan leaves (optional) - 3

Kaya toast
White sandwich bread - 4 slices
Kaya - 40g
Butter - 20g to 40g

Half-boiled eggs
Eggs - 2 
Light soy sauce - 10g
White pepper - A pinch

Salt

Kaya

In a pan, slowly reduce the coconut milk into coconut cream at medium-low heat, increasing the viscosity and fat percentage. Take 400ml down to 240ml. This should take 10 to 15 minutes. Don’t rush on high heat and don’t let the milk reach boiling, otherwise you risk splitting. Set aside.

In a bowl, whisk the eggs until fully combined, pass through a fine sieve, then combine well with 120g sugar until completely dissolved. Slowly heat in the bowl over simmering water while constantly stirring until slightly thickened and uniform. 10 to 15 minutes.

Add the coconut cream and knotted panda leaves (if using) and continue stirring and heating, don’t allow to boil. If you have a thermometer, you’re looking to increase the temperature of the mixture to 80°C (180°F) and then keep it between 80°C (180°F) and 90°C (195°F) until it thickens to the point it can coat a spoon like in the video. Around 20 to 30 minutes.

Separately, add 30g of sugar to a saucepan, spread it evenly across the pan. Heat slowly until completely caramelised without stirring. Be careful of burning, a few bubbles are fine like in the video but you want to be careful not to overdo it. Once liquid, pour into the kayak while stirring. It may solidify temporarily but if you keep stirring while hot, it will combine. Season with a small pinch of salt and set aside to cool.

Eggs

Boil some water, then add 2 eggs. Let them sit in the water undisturbed for 6.5 minutes, then remove to cool slightly. Crack open and spoon into a small bowl, season with soy sauce and white pepper.

Kaya toast (2 sandwiches)

Toast slices of white bread in butter, then remove the crusts, spread with kaya, add 2 slices of butter to each sandwich and season with salt if your butter is unsalted. Half each sandwich.

text:
Kaya Toast & Onsen Eggs 🍳🇸🇬
This is how they have em in Singapore.
With eggs in the fridge, no man is poor!

Onsen Egg Hack (No Sous Vide Machine)
Ingredients:
* 2 eggs fridge cold
* 750ml boiling water
* Soy sauce
* Black pepper
* Spring onion, thinly sliced

Method:
1. Place 2 fridge cold eggs into a ceramic bowl.
2. Pour over 700ml of boiling water (this should fully cover the eggs).
3. Cover with a plate & leave for 18 minutes.
4. Crack into a bowl season with soy sauce, black pepper & spring onions.

Note: Results may vary depending on your egg size and bowl. 
You might need some trial & error to nail it, but this should give you a good starting point! 🫡

Kaya Toast
* Toast
* Kaya (kinda like a coconut jam,  they had it at Woolies & Coles)
* Cold salted butter

Spread the kaya jam onto the toast, add thick slabs of cold salted butter, cut into soldiers then dunk into those beautiful runny eggs.

Sweet, salty, buttery…
Happy days!

Life on the Fried Side Day 321🔥
An egg each day, a different way🫡

#KayaToast #OnsenEggs #EggRecipes #BreakfastIdeas #SingaporeFood

🇲🇾Dulu Dulu✨A Modern Kopitiam in a 70-Year-Old Heritage Building❤️

Have you ever wondered how a 70-year-old building could be transformed into something special🥹Located in PJ, Dulu Dulu is a charming kopitiam that brings together nostalgic old-school flavours and a modern vibe🌟

From the outside, it retains the nostalgic charm of a traditional kopitiam, while the interior offers a cosy and comfortable space perfect for gathering with family and friends🙀

What makes it even more special is their creative twist on a local favourite kaya toast🥰Here, you can enjoy unique fillings like matcha, hojicha and sea salt pistachio🤩Their must-tries also include Chick & Toast and Nasi Ayam Masak Merah😍

For drinks and desserts, don't miss their Jasmine Yuan Yang Tau Fu Fa, Matcha Gula Melaka Tau Fu Fa and Cendol Bingsu🥹

If you're looking for a kopitiam experience that combines nostalgic charm with a modern touch, Dulu Dulu is definitely worth a visit❤️

【Dulu Dulu】
📍40, Jalan 52/18, Bandar Baru Petaling Jaya, 46200 Petaling Jaya
⏰10.30AM - 10PM (Closed on Monday)

🧈 10/10 Recommended 🧈

📍 Bao Er Cafe • Multiple outlets islandwide, details below!

Omg… easily the BEST kaya toast I’ve had recently 😍

Here’s what I ordered:
🥥 Kaya Toast Set (comes with 2 eggs + kopi)
🥜 Peanut Toast
🧈 Extra butter
🥥 Extra kaya

Let me explain why this slaps — the toast is thin but fluffy and airy, perfectly pan-grilled so every bite is crisp on the outside yet soft inside. The house-made kaya is fragrant and creamy, rich with coconut that lingers beautifully.

Dip it into your runny egg + a dash of soya + white pepper and you unlock a whole new level — that umami from the soya and the gentle heat from white pepper just elevate the whole experience so well 👌🏻

Honestly, kaya toast done right can make every morning better.

• Fortune Center, Mon – Sun • 8:00am – 8:00pm  
• Balestier Plaza, Mon – Sun • 8:00am – 8:00pm

text:
Kay tagal kong hinintay tong moment na to...Nung una ko tong natikman to sa SG, dinagdag ko na agad sa listahan ng mga paborito ko. 

Love at first bite.... 😍

Hindi pretentious yung place. Sakto lang. Malinis din.

Serving time: super speed, halos 5 mins lang. Kaso ako lang tao nun. Baka naman.

What I ordered for my lovely self: kaya toast with butter (comes with hot coffee, kung gusto mo iced + P20). Basta, total bill ko 200. 

Nakakabusog sa hungry ferson with a normal appetite. Unang kagat ko, ramdam ko yung crunch ng tinapay...tapos lasa ko yung magandang contrast ng sweet and coconut taste ng kaya jam + salty / creaminess ng butter. Hay heaven. Sawsaw mo pa sa mekus mekus dip. Di ko na maexplain ung lasa. Try mo nalang. Basta sakin overall, nagmamake sense lahat kahit mukhang hindi. 

Yung kape, unang sip ko, ramdam ko yung sipa sa utak kong sabaw @ 2:30pm.

Sa tingin ko, super sulit dito.
Shur babalikbalikan.
#fyp

text:
have you tried breakfast from this old-school coffeeshop in Singapore? ☕️🍞

I first came across this place through a tourist’s recommendation on TikTok, and I never knew this was such a hidden gem. It’s not your usual coffee shop, a lot of the old-school elements were preserved, you can see vintage photos / items from the past and even the bread was toasted on a charcoal grill. 

The bread is also not what you typically get at your usual Singaporean breakfast coffee shops, because it’s the really old-school white bread which is soft and fluffy and I think it’s the best pairing with the soft boiled eggs and nanyang kopi. 

I wasn’t expecting to end off my meal with the curry puff, but damn… it was so good, the crust is thin and the filling was piping hot. If you like sardines, I definitely recommend the sardine puff! 

It was actually refreshing and nice to rediscover this side of Singapore which I honestly never knew existed and I do hope more locals will get to try out this breakfast spot whenever you have the chance to! Do note that the parking can be quite limited 👀

📍Heap Seng Leong
10 N Bridge Rd, Unit 01-5109, Singapore 190010

text:
From hawker centres, kopitiams, or chains around Singapore, the breakfast combo of kaya toast, soft boiled eggs, and kopi (coffee) is an absolute classic. 

Kaya is a coconut jam, made with coconut milk, egg yolks, sugar, and the Malay version also has pandan leaves for added flavor. 

I love a bit of food history, so this satisfied that itch for me. It also goes to show how recipes we make everyday or food we have on the regular is actually knowledge we've passed down for generations prior, and will continue to evolve for generations to come. 

#singapore #foodhistory  #kaya #kayatoast
